findings.claim: The decision keeps the no-HTTPS conclusion even though a stated falsifier already fired against the premise that the chosen substrate is usable for mobile today.
findings.evidence: Falsifier 3 says: "RUN 2026-08-01. IT FIRED" and "A phone on the same network cannot reach the daemon today." The document then preserves the decision anyway: "What survives is narrower and still correct — sovereign-sync is the right transport... so the decision stands while its scope shrinks."
findings.suggested_fix: Do not commit to "Do not build a signed HTTPS bundle fetcher" until the binding/exposure decision is made and a phone can actually reach and update through sovereign-sync.

findings.claim: The decision depends on an explicitly unverified assumption that the synced index is sufficient to make skills usable, which directly determines whether an additional content transport is required.
findings.evidence: Assumption: "skill-index carries enough to update a device... it is unverified whether a device can reconstruct a usable pack from the synced entries alone, or whether it also needs skill bodies." Falsifier 2 admits: "If bodies are missing, a content transport is still required."
findings.suggested_fix: Run the empty-pack sync test before committing; if skill bodies are required, decide the content transport separately rather than banning the HTTPS bundle path.

findings.claim: The first falsifier identifies a case where HTTPS may be required, but the decision does not bound whether that case is in or out of scope.
findings.evidence: Falsifier 1: "A device with no paired desktop and no peer cannot update at all... If it cannot, the HTTPS bundle stops being redundant and becomes the offline path — this decision then covers only the paired case." The Decision section still states broadly: "Do not build a signed HTTPS bundle fetcher."
findings.suggested_fix: State whether unpaired/no-peer mobile update is a required scenario. If it is required, this decision is not justified; if it is excluded, restrict the decision title and scope to paired/peer-available updates.

findings.claim: The same decision topic/id already appears in prior decisions, but the document does not acknowledge whether this is an amendment, replacement, or duplicate decision.
findings.evidence: prior_decisions includes "[decision-mobile-update-transport] Decision: mobile skill updates ride sovereign-sync, not a signed HTTPS bundle — tags: decision, outcome-pending" while the target is also ".prometheus/knowledge/wiki/decision-mobile-update-transport.md" with id "decision-mobile-update-transport".
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the document as an update/amendment to the existing decision, record what changed, and preserve the old outcome/status rather than silently re-deciding the same ground.

findings.claim: The decision assumes LAN/mobile bearer-token exposure is acceptable without addressing the new security boundary created by making the daemon reachable from a phone.
findings.evidence: Assumption: "A mobile client can hold a bearer token... not exercised from an actual device here." Falsifier 3 concludes sovereign-sync "needs a binding/exposure decision before a mobile host can use it" after showing the daemon is currently loopback-only.
findings.suggested_fix: Before choosing LAN-exposed sovereign-sync over HTTPS, define authentication, token storage, rotation/revocation, and network exposure requirements for the mobile daemon path.

findings.claim: The CRDT assumption is unresolved for destructive pack updates, so the chosen substrate may have wrong semantics for removals or upgrades.
findings.evidence: Assumption: "CRDT merge is the right semantic for a skill catalogue... untested for a pack upgrade that removes skills."
findings.suggested_fix: Specify and test deletion/tombstone/version semantics for skill pack upgrades before treating sovereign-sync as the update transport.
